qa_pairs.question: How do I configure LS-DYNA to use an Ansys license server when running jobs on Alliance clusters?
qa_pairs.answer: To configure LS-DYNA with an Ansys license server, you must set the environment variables `LSTC_LICENSE=ansys` and `ANSYSLMD_LICENSE_FILE=<port>@<server>` in your Slurm scripts, replacing `<port>` with an integer number and `<server>` with the hostname or IP address of your Ansys license server. It is also required that a file named `~/.licenses/ls-dyna.lic` exists (even if empty) for the `ls-dyna` module to load, which you can ensure by running `touch ~/.licenses/ls-dyna.lic` once from the command line or each time in your Slurm scripts. Only module versions 12.2.1 or newer are compatible with Ansys license servers.

qa_pairs.question: What are the capabilities and limitations of the SHARCNET Ansys license for LS-DYNA available to Alliance researchers?
qa_pairs.answer: The SHARCNET Ansys license supports running single-node SMP (Shared Memory Parallel) or MPP (Message Passing Parallel) LS-DYNA jobs with many cores using the `dysmp` license feature. However, it does not support multi-node distributed memory MPP LS-DYNA jobs because it lacks the `mppdyna` feature. Any Alliance researcher can freely use this license for academic research and associated publications, running up to 5 simultaneous LS-DYNA jobs with a total of 288 cores and unlimited mesh size. To utilize it, include `export LSTC_LICENSE=ansys` and `export ANSYSLMD_LICENSE_FILE=1055@license1.computecanada.ca` in your Slurm script.
